Hosting playbook

Eurovision night — host the perfect watch party

Eurovision night is the annual living-room ritual where you watch the Eurovision Song Contest with friends, rate every song, and argue about which country deserves to win. This guide turns it from passive viewing into a competitive, scored party game using Eurovision Games — a free browser-based companion that handles predictions, trivia, and scoring while you watch.

If you're hosting cross-country, align on the host's local kick-off and start the room 30 minutes earlier.

Guide

How to host (10-step playbook)

  1. 1

    Pick a venue

    Living room, garden, projector on a wall — or a Zoom/FaceTime call if you're scattered.

  2. 2

    Confirm the broadcast

    National broadcaster (BBC One, ARD, ERT, RAI, etc.) or the official YouTube live-stream where licensing allows.

  3. 3

    Send a save-the-date

    Doors open ~1 hour before kick-off so guests can settle in, join the room and start their predictions.

  4. 4

    Open Eurovision GamesIn the game

    Create a room at eurovision.games on the host's phone or laptop, share the join link and tap Start the Party! once everyone is in.

  5. 5

    Set the lineup

    Print or screenshot the 2026 running order so everyone has a reference for predictions.

  6. 6

    Make predictionsIn the game

    Every guest picks Top 5 and Worst 5 — ideally before the first song. Picks stay editable until voting opens, when the app locks them.

  7. 7

    Watch song-by-song

    React, score, take photos. Encourage opinionated commentary.

  8. 8

    Use breaks for trivia duelsIn the game

    The interval act is ~25 minutes — perfect duel window.

  9. 9

    Watch the vote

    Jury vote first, then televote — the most chaotic 25 minutes of TV all year.

  10. 10

    Crown winnersIn the game

    After the televote, the app reveals five trophy cards — Champion, Thief, Duelist, Oracle, Guru.

Inside the room

Game options inside the room

  • Predictions

    Top 5, Worst 5 — editable until voting opens, then locked and scored automatically against jury + televote.

  • Trivia duels

    Head-to-head between any two players. The winner steals their duel score from the loser or doubles it for themselves. Each of you can challenge the other once, plus one rematch for the loser — so nobody grinds one opponent.

  • Quiz rounds

    Three rapid-fire rounds each player plays at their own pace, from party start until voting opens.

  • Sudden-death tiebreak

    Optional. If players tie a winner category, the room votes — Accept (share the trophy) or Sudden Death. If Sudden Death wins, the tied players fight through a 3-question trivia match.

Time-zone tips

Grand final start times vary by country: 21:00 CEST (Germany, France, Spain), 20:00 BST/UTC+1 (UK, Ireland), 22:00 EEST (Greece, Cyprus, Finland, Israel), 05:00 AEST next morning (Australia — record it). If you're hosting cross-country, align on the host's local kick-off and start the room 30 minutes earlier.

What is Eurovision night?

Eurovision night is the live grand-final broadcast of the Eurovision Song Contest, held on a Saturday in mid-May each year. In 2026 the grand final airs on Saturday 16 May 2026 from Vienna, with semi-finals earlier that week. Across Europe (and Australia) it is a single televised live event watched by ~160 million people; in homes it has become a competitive social event, a costume party, and a drinking game all at once.

Food and drink ideas

The classic move: one snack per favourite country. Sweden = meatballs and Daim. Italy = arancini. Greece = souvlaki. UK = sausage rolls. Don't over-cater — the focus is the screen. A flexible buffet that survives the 4-hour run-time beats a hot served dinner. Mocktails travel well; an alcohol-free option keeps drivers and non-drinkers happy through to the televote.
